fix: Use fmt::Write (add `use std::fmt::Write as _;` at the top of the module) and write into the buffer directly, removing the temporary String and the `"  ".repeat(..)` allocation. Depth-limit branch: `let _ = writeln!(output, "{:width$}… semantic dump truncated (depth limit)", "", width = max_depth.min(256) * 2);`. Node line: `let _ = writeln!(output, "{:width$}{:?}#{:?} label={:?} value={:?} bounds=({:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1}) focused={} actions={:?}", "", node.role, node.id, truncate(...), truncate(...), node.bounds.origin.x, node.bounds.origin.y, node.bounds.size.width, node.bounds.size.height, node.state.focused, node.actions, width = depth.saturating_mul(2));`. Output bytes are identical (two spaces per depth level). `let _ =` is fine because writes to a String cannot fail.

Take the borrowed text form: `fn truncate(value: Option<&str>, max_chars: usize) -> Option<String>` and call it with `node.label.as_deref()` / `node.value.as_deref()` at the two call sites (lines 611-612). The body is unchanged apart from the `value.clone()` becoming `value.to_owned()`.
Use `extra.sort_unstable_by_key(|id| id.0);`. The keys are arena ids, which are unique, so no two elements compare equal and the result is identical to the stable sort.
